'''Guy Philip Nason''' (born 28 August 1966)<ref>[http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/article/oupww/whoswho/U249654 NASON, Prof. Guy Philip], ''Who's Who 2014'', A & C Black, 2014; online edn, Oxford University Press, 2014</ref> is a British statistician, and professor of Statistics at [[Imperial College London]].

Nason received his BSc from the [[University of Bath]] in 1988, a diploma in Mathematical Statistics from the [[University of Cambridge]] in 1989, and a PhD in Statistics from the [[University of Bath]] in 1992. He served as a Council member of the [[Royal Statistical Society]] (2004–08), and was Vice-President (Academic Affairs) 2016–2020. He is a member of the [[EPSRC]] Strategic Advisory Team for Mathematics. He was an [[EPSRC]] Advanced Research Fellow during 2000–5 and was awarded the [[Guy Medal]] in bronze by the [[Royal Statistical Society]] (RSS) in 2001.<ref>[http://www.stat.colostate.edu/graybillconference2006/abstracts.htm Abstracts and speaker biographies], Graybill Conference, 11–13 June 2006, [[Colorado State University]]. Accessed 15 August 2011</ref><ref>[http://www.rss.org.uk/site/cms/contentviewarticle.asp?article=479 Previous award recipients] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120317045440/http://www.rss.org.uk/site/cms/contentviewarticle.asp?article=479 |date=17 March 2012 }},   [[Royal Statistical Society]] . Accessed 15 August 2011</ref> He took over the post as head of mathematics at Bristol from [[Stephen Wiggins]] in 2008.

Nason is best known for his work in the area of [[time series analysis]], especially [[wavelet]] approaches.<ref>G. P. Nason & R. von Sachs "Wavelets in Time Series Analysis" Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London A, 1999, 357, 2511–2526</ref><ref>G.P. Nason, R von Sachs & G Kroisandt "Wavelet processes and adaptive estimation of the evolutionary wavelet spectrum." [[Journal of the Royal Statistical Society]], Series B, 2000, 62, 271–292</ref><ref>G. P. Nason ''Wavelet Methods in Statistics with R (Use R)'', Springer-Verlag, {{ISBN|0-387-75960-3}}</ref>
He has served as the Secretary of the RSS Research Section (2002–04), associate editor for the Journal of the RSS, Series B, Computational Statistics and Statistica Sinica and is currently an associate editor for ''[[Biometrika]]''.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20120405125658/http://www.oxfordjournals.org/our_journals/biomet/editorial_board.html Editorial Board],  ''[[Biometrika]]''. Accessed 5 September 2011</ref>
